records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, October 17, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Androgens amplify SARS-CoV-2 inflammation while estrogen restrains it by October 17, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 8 mins read 0 Androgens amplify SARS-CoV-2 inflammation while estrogen restrains it Get Fit Guides Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Biological sex has long been recognized as a determinant of how severely coronavirus disease 2019 progresses, with male patients consistently showing higher rates of hypoxemic respiratory failure, hyperinflammation, and mortality. Low testosterone concentrations in hospitalized men correlate with elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly interleukin-6, and progressive testosterone decline accompanied by rising interleukin-10 levels tracks with increasing disease severity and death risk. Elevated estradiol-to-testosterone ratios, conversely, are associated with hyperinflammatory states and higher hospital mortality. Yet the molecular machinery through which sex steroids regulate immune and endothelial responses to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has remained only partially characterized. A new study published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology by Sandra Bižić-Radulović of the University Clinical Center of Serbia and colleagues now provides detailed mechanistic evidence that androgenic and estrogenic signaling exert opposing, cell-type-specific effects on virus-induced inflammatory pathways. The research team hypothesized that β-estradiol and dihydrotestosterone (DHT), the most potent androgen, would differentially modulate inflammatory signaling and monocyte–endothelial interactions during SARS-CoV-2 exposure. To test this, they exposed HULEC-5a lung microvascular endothelial cells, THP-1 monocytic leukemia cells, and primary monocytes and neutrophils isolated from patients with confirmed COVID-19 to in vitro-amplified Wuhan-1 SARS-CoV-2 at a multiplicity of infection of 0.001 for 24 and 48 hours. All procedures involving live virus were conducted in a certified Biosafety Level 3 laboratory in accordance with institutional biosafety regulations and World Health Organization recommendations. Cells were treated with DHT, β-estradiol, or the androgen receptor antagonist flutamide at nanomolar to micromolar concentrations before viral exposure. Receptor gene expression was measured by RT-qPCR, inflammatory signaling by Western blot against phosphorylated and total NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK proteins, and monocyte transendothelial migration by Boyden chamber assay. Patient samples were collected between June 2020 and April 2022 at the Clinic for Infectious and Tropical Diseases of the University Clinical Center of Serbia. Get Fit Guides The first key finding concerns how SARS-CoV-2 itself reshapes the expression of sex steroid receptors in a cell-specific manner. The virus reduced expression of estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1) in endothelial cells after 24 hours (p<0.05), while simultaneously increasing ESR1 expression in neutrophils (p<0.05) and monocytes (p<0.01) from patients with COVID-19. Androgen receptor (AR) expression was inversely regulated in neutrophils and monocytes: the virus reduced AR in neutrophils after 24 hours (p<0.001) but increased it in monocytes (p<0.05). These differential patterns suggest that SARS-CoV-2 actively reprograms the hormonal responsiveness of both vascular and immune compartments. The authors propose that suppression of ESR1 in endothelial cells may contribute to endothelial dysfunction, vascular inflammation, and thrombotic complications of severe disease, whereas increased ESR1 in circulating innate immune cells may represent a compensatory immunoregulatory response to systemic inflammation. Get Rapid Tests Discover more Study Biology See an OB-GYN Get Fit Guides Track Fertility Find Specialists In THP-1 monocytic cells, SARS-CoV-2 generally activated inflammatory signaling pathways including NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK, with activation reaching up to 1.9-fold above baseline. The NFκB response was further augmented by DHT (44.6%) and attenuated by flutamide (44.1%), indicating that androgen receptor signaling amplifies a central mediator of virus-induced cytokine production. STAT3 signaling was also activated by the virus (p<0.01), and both AR activation and AR blockade were associated with sustained STAT3 phosphorylation at 48 hours, though with different temporal dynamics: the DHT-associated increase at 48 hours was 3.4-fold lower than at 24 hours, whereas the flutamide-associated level remained unchanged between the two time points. Prolonged p38 MAPK activation was maintained by a low dose of DHT (10 nM) and reduced by low-dose flutamide (100 nM), but not by higher flutamide concentrations, suggesting dose-dependent and pathway-specific modulation of inflammatory cascades by androgen-responsive mechanisms. Study Biology In HULEC-5a lung endothelial cells of human male origin, the picture was notably different. SARS-CoV-2 reduced STAT3 activation at 24 hours (p<0.05), an effect not further modified by DHT or flutamide. After 48 hours, DHT alone reduced STAT3 activation even in the absence of virus (p<0.01), indicating a direct effect of androgen signaling on baseline STAT3 activity in endothelial cells. In SARS-CoV-2-exposed cells, DHT twice reduced virus-induced activation of the p38 MAPK pathway (p<0.05). These results suggest that androgen signaling can partially suppress inflammatory signaling in endothelial cells both at baseline and during viral exposure, a finding that contrasts with the amplifying effects observed in monocytic cells and underscores the highly cell-specific nature of sex steroid immunoregulation during SARS-CoV-2 infection. Discover more Find Treatments Get Rapid Tests Read Med Journals Primary immune cells from patients with COVID-19 revealed further complexity. In neutrophils, β-estradiol inhibited NFκB signaling 2.2-fold, whereas DHT stimulated it 4.9-fold. SARS-CoV-2 reduced NFκB activation in neutrophils from female patients after 24 hours (p<0.001), and β-estradiol further reduced NFκB activation in a dose-dependent manner irrespective of viral exposure (p<0.01). In contrast, DHT increased NFκB activation after 48 hours independently of SARS-CoV-2. Simultaneously, the virus strongly induced p38 MAPK activation in neutrophils (>10-fold) after 24 hours (p<0.001). The authors note that persistent p38 MAPK activation may sustain neutrophil activation despite partial NFκB inhibition, contributing to oxidative stress, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, and tissue damage associated with severe disease. They also highlight that G protein-coupled estrogen receptor 1 (GPER1), a membrane-associated estrogen receptor expressed in human monocytes and neutrophils, may regulate neutrophil inflammatory responses through cAMP/PKA/CREB and MAPK signaling pathways. Get Rapid Tests In monocytes from patients with COVID-19, DHT at 1 nM enhanced NFκB activation in the presence of SARS-CoV-2 after 24 hours (p<0.05), while β-estradiol at 100 nM increased p38 MAPK activation (p<0.01) and at the lowest concentration tested (1 nM) increased p38 MAPK activation irrespective of viral exposure (p<0.05). Comparison of exposure durations showed stronger SARS-CoV-2-induced activation of NFκB and p38 MAPK after 24 hours than after 48 hours (p<0.05), indicating a transient but pronounced activation of these pathways during early viral exposure. Notably, SARS-CoV-2 activation of inflammatory signaling deteriorates over time in monocytes from patients with COVID-19 (p<0.05), suggesting that androgen-mediated amplification of NFκB and MAPK cascades may contribute to exaggerated innate immune activation and heightened inflammatory responses in male patients with severe disease. Perhaps the most functionally significant results emerged from the Boyden chamber migration assay. DHT significantly increased trans-endothelial migration of monocytes from patients with COVID-19 (p<0.001) and promoted detachment of SARS-CoV-2-exposed HULEC-5a endothelial cells (p<0.01). Monocyte migration through SARS-CoV-2-exposed endothelial layers was predominantly enhanced by DHT and, to a lesser extent, by β-estradiol and flutamide (p<0.001). After correction for endothelial background fluorescence and monocyte-only controls, increased migration remained evident, particularly in DHT-treated conditions. These findings suggest that androgen signaling promotes endothelial dysfunction and facilitates monocyte transmigration during SARS-CoV-2 infection, key events in COVID-19-associated immunothrombosis and vascular injury. Enhanced leukocyte trafficking across the endothelial barrier may promote tissue infiltration by inflammatory cells and aggravate local cytokine production. The authors acknowledge limitations, including that sex-stratified analyses were not uniformly performed across all experiments involving primary immune cells because of limited availability of freshly isolated samples, and that the use of HULEC-5a cells derived from a single male donor restricts assessment of sex-dependent differences in endothelial responses. Nevertheless, the findings elucidate molecular mechanisms driving male-biased COVID-19 severity and underscore the potential of targeting androgen-responsive pathways as a therapeutic strategy to mitigate severe viral inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Beyond SARS-CoV-2, the differential regulation of NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK pathways observed here may reflect fundamental mechanisms of sex hormone-mediated immunoregulation that extend to other immune-mediated and vascular diseases in which sex steroids contribute to disease susceptibility and progression. The study’s experimental design merits closer attention because it bridges two levels of analysis that are often treated separately in COVID-19 research: controlled cell-line experiments and primary cells drawn from acutely ill patients. By using the same Wuhan-1 viral stock, verified by sequencing and titrated by TCID50 and plaque assay, for every condition, the investigators minimized viral preparation as a confounding variable. The low multiplicity of infection of 0.001 is notable, as it means relatively few cells received productive viral input, yet robust signaling changes were still detectable. This suggests that even limited viral exposure can trigger substantial inflammatory pathway activation, consistent with the idea that a small number of infected cells can amplify responses through paracrine signaling, although the study did not directly test such amplification mechanisms. The choice of signaling readouts also connects the findings to established COVID-19 biology. NFκB is the canonical transcription factor driving transcription of tumor necrosis factor, interleukin-6, and interleukin-1 family cytokines, all of which are elevated in severe disease and correlate with the testosterone deficits described in the clinical literature. STAT3 links cytokine signaling, particularly through the interleukin-6 receptor JAK-STAT axis, to cell survival and inflammatory differentiation programs in monocytes and neutrophils. p38 MAPK is a stress-activated kinase implicated in cytokine translation, oxidative burst, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation. The observation that SARS-CoV-2 activated all three pathways in monocytic cells, and that androgen receptor agonism and antagonism shifted the magnitude of these responses in opposite directions, provides a mechanistic scaffold for interpreting why male patients with lower testosterone might nonetheless experience androgen-driven hyperinflammation, since DHT effects were observed at concentrations within the physiological range. The dose-dependence of the androgen effects deserves particular emphasis. In the THP-1 experiments, low-dose DHT at 10 nanomolar sustained p38 MAPK activation while low-dose flutamide at 100 nanomolar reduced it, but higher flutamide concentrations did not reproduce this effect. Such non-monotonic dose relationships are a recognized feature of sex steroid biology, where receptor occupancy, receptor isoform expression, and co-regulator availability can produce qualitatively different outcomes at different ligand concentrations. For translational purposes, this complexity cautions against simple assumptions that androgen blockade will uniformly suppress inflammatory signaling across all cell types and doses, and it highlights the need for careful pharmacological characterization before any therapeutic repurposing of androgen receptor antagonists in viral disease. The cell-type specificity of the findings is equally important. DHT amplified NFκB signaling in monocytic cells and neutrophils, yet it twice reduced virus-induced p38 MAPK activation in endothelial cells and lowered baseline STAT3 activity after 48 hours. This divergence means that androgen signaling cannot be characterized as simply pro- or anti-inflammatory; rather, its net effect on systemic inflammation depends on the relative contribution of vascular versus immune compartments to a given clinical phenotype. In severe COVID-19, where both endothelial injury and myeloid cell hyperactivation drive pathology, the opposing effects could partially offset each other or, alternatively, the monocyte- and neutrophil-directed amplification may dominate because these cells produce the circulating cytokines and tissue-damaging mediators observed in patients. The transendothelial migration results add a functional dimension that goes beyond signaling biochemistry. Monocyte recruitment across the endothelial barrier is a hallmark of vascular inflammation and contributes directly to immunothrombosis, the process by which leukocyte activation, tissue factor expression, and platelet engagement generate thrombi in the pulmonary and systemic microvasculature. The finding that DHT promoted monocyte migration with high statistical significance, and that it also induced detachment of virus-exposed endothelial cells, links androgen signaling to two mechanistically connected events: weakening of the endothelial monolayer and enhanced leukocyte trafficking through it. Detachment of endothelial cells, if it occurs in vivo, could expose subendothelial matrix and tissue factor, providing a procoagulant surface that complements the inflammatory effects of infiltrating monocytes. The differential regulation of estrogen receptor expression by the virus itself adds another layer of interpretation. Reduced ESR1 in endothelial cells could diminish the protective, anti-inflammatory tone that estrogen signaling normally provides to the vasculature, including nitric oxide-mediated vasodilation and suppression of adhesion molecule expression. Increased ESR1 in neutrophils and monocytes, conversely, might represent a compensatory attempt by innate immune cells to enhance estrogen-dependent immunoregulation during systemic inflammation. Whether this compensatory upregulation is functionally effective in patients, or is overwhelmed by the concurrent androgen-driven amplification of NFκB and MAPK signaling, remains an open question that would require measuring receptor protein levels and downstream estrogen-responsive gene expression in patient cells. The temporal dimension of the findings, with stronger pathway activation at 24 hours than at 48 hours in patient monocytes and progressive deterioration of inflammatory signaling over the course of disease, aligns with clinical observations that COVID-19 inflammation evolves in phases. Early innate immune activation, followed by sustained or dysregulated myeloid responses, characterizes progression toward severe disease. The observation that signaling responses in patient monocytes worsened over time suggests that longitudinal sampling, rather than single time-point measurements, may be necessary to capture the full trajectory of sex steroid modulation in COVID-19, and it raises the possibility that therapeutic timing, whether targeting androgen signaling early or late in disease, could substantially influence outcomes. Finally, the study’s reliance on the Wuhan-1 variant, collected during the first years of the pandemic, invites consideration of how these mechanisms might apply to later variants with altered inflammatory profiles. The core signaling pathways investigated here, NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK, are activated by multiple pattern recognition receptors and cytokine circuits, so the sex steroid modulation described is unlikely to be variant-specific in principle. However, the magnitude of viral replication, the efficiency of cell entry, and the specific cytokine milieu induced by different variants could shift the balance between androgen-amplified and estrogen-attenuated responses. Extending this experimental framework to contemporary variants, and to cells from vaccinated individuals with pre-existing adaptive immunity, would help determine whether the androgen-responsive mechanisms identified here remain relevant targets for mitigating severe viral inflammation and endothelial dysfunction in current clinical practice. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, October 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Technology Sugar Coats Near the Furin Site Steer SARS-CoV-2 Spike Processing Across Variants by October 16, 2026 in Technology Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Sugar Coats Near the Furin Site Steer SARS-CoV-2 Spike Processing Across Variants Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram The SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein has been dissected in extraordinary detail since 2020, yet new work from a team at the Center for Infection and Immunity of Lille shows that some of the most consequential features of this molecular machine lie not in its receptor-binding domains or mutation hotspots, but in the sugar chains clustered just upstream of the site where the protein must be cut. The study, published in Scientific Reports, demonstrates that three N-linked glycans positioned near the S1/S2 boundary — at asparagine residues 603, 616 and 657 — exert a decisive influence on how the spike is processed by host proteases, and that this influence has shifted measurably as the virus has evolved from the ancestral D614 lineage through G614 and into the Omicron XBB.1.5 variant. The spike protein is the multimeric engine of coronavirus entry. Its larger S1 subunit carries the receptor-binding machinery that latches onto ACE2 on the surface of human cells, while the smaller S2 subunit is the fusogenic core that, once triggered, refolds to drive merger of the viral envelope with the host cell membrane. Between these two subunits sits a polybasic cleavage motif, the RRAR sequence that distinguishes SARS-CoV-2 from many related coronaviruses and that is recognised and cut by furin and other proprotein convertases within the producing cell. This cleavage event, termed priming, is not decorative: it pre-activates the spike so that the virus is poised for rapid membrane fusion upon receptor engagement, a property widely credited with contributing to efficient human-to-human transmission. What makes the region around the cleavage site chemically complex is that the spike is one of the most heavily glycosylated proteins known in virology, carrying 22 N-linked glycans per protomer. These carbohydrates serve the canonical functions of shielding immunodominant epitopes and escorting the protein through the folding and quality-control machinery of the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus. But several of the glycosylation sequons sit remarkably close to the S1/S2 junction, raising a long-standing question: do these sugars physically modulate access of furin to the polybasic motif, and if so, does removing them cripple the entry functions of the spike? To answer this, Muriel Lavie, Emma Louvet, Jules Patron, Xavier Hanoulle and Sandrine Belouzard systematically mutated the asparagine residues at positions 603, 616 and 657, individually and in combination, thereby ablating the corresponding N-glycans without otherwise altering the spike sequence. They then measured three tightly linked readouts in cell systems: the efficiency with which the spike was cleaved into its S1 and S2 subunits, the capacity of the processed spike to mediate cell–cell fusion, and its ability to support entry of pseudotyped particles into target cells expressing ACE2. The comparative dimension of the design is what gives the work its evolutionary punch, because the same mutant panel was assessed on two distinct genetic backgrounds: the D614 variant and its G614 descendant that rapidly became globally dominant in 2020, and the XBB.1.5 Omicron variant that circulated widely in 2023. The first major finding concerns a compensatory basic residue. When the three glycans were removed simultaneously, cleavage of the spike did not simply collapse; instead, the authors found that processing of the glycan-deficient spike became dependent on arginine at position 634, a basic residue lying within the cleavage-proximal region. In other words, the loss of the sugar shield exposed a functional redundancy in the local sequence: with the glycans gone, the enzymatic machinery that processes the spike leans on the R634 residue to achieve productive cutting. This interplay between carbohydrate occupancy and a specific cationic side chain underscores how finely balanced the protease-recognition landscape around the S1/S2 junction really is, and it suggests that the local electrostatic and steric environment — not merely the canonical RRAR motif — determines whether priming occurs efficiently. The second finding is that on the D614 and G614 backgrounds, the glycans at 603, 616 and 657 and the R634 residue are each required for full fusion and entry competence. Mutating these positions on those variants produced measurable deficits in both cell–cell fusion assays and pseudotype entry, indicating that the glycan cluster and the compensatory basic residue act in concert to maintain the entry functions that follow successful cleavage. The consistency across D614 and G614 is notable because the G614 substitution itself is known to stabilise the spike and increase its incorporation into virions; the new data indicate that even on that stabilised backbone, the cleavage-site glycans remain non-negotiable structural elements. The picture changes, however, when the same experiments are repeated on XBB.1.5. In the Omicron background, mutations of the three glycosylation sites and of R634 had a milder impact on spike processing and entry functions than they did in the ancestral variants. The authors conclude from this pattern that the functional roles of N603, N616, N657 and R634 have evolved alongside the circulating variants. This is a subtle but important point for evolutionary virology: Omicron lineages accumulated dozens of changes across the spike, including extensive remodeling of the receptor-binding domain and adjustments near the S1/S2 region, and the new results show that these changes have partially uncoupled entry competence from the glycan-and-arginine dependency that governed earlier forms of the virus. Mechanistically, the results fit a model in which the upstream glycans act as steric modulators of furin accessibility. Bulky N-linked carbohydrates projecting from the peptide backbone around residues 603 to 657 can either occlude or funnel the protease toward the polybasic motif, depending on their precise position and occupancy. Removing them appears to perturb the local conformation in a way that shifts the burden of recognition onto nearby basic residues such as R634. At the same time, the glycans’ contribution to fusion and entry in D614 and G614 suggests they do more than merely regulate cleavage access; they may help stabilise the metastable pre-fusion architecture that the S2 subunit must maintain until the moment of triggering. Their reduced importance in XBB.1.5 implies that other sequence features of the Omicron spike have taken over some of that stabilising or presenting role. The work also carries implications that extend beyond SARS-CoV-2 itself. The dependence of proteolytic priming on glycan context echoes findings in other enveloped viruses, where carbohydrates adjacent to cleavage sites modulate activation of fusion proteins. For coronavirus surveillance, the message is that mutations at N-glycosylation sequons near the S1/S2 boundary should not be dismissed as neutral surface noise; depending on the genetic background in which they appear, they can reshape how efficiently the spike is primed and how readily the virus enters cells. Conversely, the variant-dependent behaviour means that any prediction of a glycan mutation’s effect must account for the rest of the spike sequence — a caution against interpreting such changes in isolation. For therapeutic and vaccine design, the study adds a further layer of nuance. Glycan-shielded regions of the spike are notoriously difficult targets for antibody-based countermeasures, but understanding which sugars are functionally load-bearing, and how their roles shift between variants, can inform the design of stabilized immunogens and small molecules that target the cleavage-proximal region. The Lille team’s findings, supported by the region Hauts-de-France through the REACT’EU programme and conducted with the imaging facilities of the BioImaging Center Lille Nord-de-France, reinforce a theme that has run through coronavirus structural biology since the pandemic began: the spike is not a static target but a dynamically glycosylated, protease-regulated machine, and its evolution must be read through that lens. As SARS-CoV-2 continues to diversify, the sugar chains flanking its activation switch may yet prove to be among the quiet arbiters of which variants rise and which fade. records.content: Why do some children become seriously ill with COVID-19? The answer may lie in their genes Many of the genes our study identified were involved with immune responses. - 13 October 2026 - 4 min read - by The Conversation Most children who are infected with SARS-COV2, the virus that causes COVID, experience only mild symptoms or no symptoms at all. But a small proportion develop severe illness which can sometimes even require hospital care. The reason why only some children develop severe illness hasn’t been clear until now. But our latest study provides new insights into the immune responses associated with severe respiratory infections such as COVID. Our study analysed blood gene expression profiles from 333 South African children with similar genetic backgrounds. A gene expression profile measures the activity of thousands of genes simultaneously. Analysing them can tell us whether some genes have been switched “on” or “off” in response to an infection. Of these children, 127 were considered healthy, 71 had mild or asymptomatic COVID, 41 were hospitalised with severe COVID, 47 were hospitalised with a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection and 47 had pulmonary tuberculosis. Only children who were exposed to a single respiratory infection were included. We also adjusted our analyses for age. Our study identified thousands of genes that behaved differently in children with severe COVID and other respiratory infections compared with healthy controls. More than 5,000 genes showed altered activity in the children who were experiencing a severe respiratory infection. Many of these genes were involved in immune responses. For instance, children with severe respiratory infections exhibited stronger neutrophil responses. Neutrophils are a type of immune cell that form part of the body’s rapid, first-line of defence against infections. Similarly, interferon-gamma signalling, which is a critical pathway that helps coordinate immune responses to pathogens, was switched “on”. Interestingly, our study also found significant differences in the types of immune cells that children with severe respiratory infections had circulating in their blood. Those experiencing severe infections had significantly higher proportions of macrophages – the body’s innate immune cells. But they also had lower proportions of T cells – immune cells that coordinate overall immune response. These changes were not seen in children with mild or asymptomatic COVID or in healthy children. One of the most interesting findings was that some immune responses were shared across COVID, RSV and pulmonary tuberculosis. We identified a total of seven types of immune cells that showed similar patterns of activity across these different respiratory illnesses. This suggests that children may activate common defence mechanisms when faced with severe lung infections. At the same time, other gene expression patterns appeared to be unique to particular infections. This highlights important biological differences between diseases. Identifying responses that may help distinguish different respiratory infections would be useful, as different infections require different therapies. The study also identified 82 genes that could help distinguish a severe COVID infection from a mild or asymptomatic one. This raises the possibility that we could use gene expression signatures – which provide a snapshot of which genes are activated at a given time – to predict which children are most at risk of developing severe disease. Childhood immune responses Children with respiratory infections often arrive at hospital with very similar symptoms. Yet the biological processes driving these illnesses can be quite different. By comparing healthy children against children infected with common respiratory infections, we’re beginning to identify both the shared and unique features of childhood immune responses. Understanding these differences could eventually improve how doctors diagnose infections, monitor diseases and tailor treatments. Some of the genes highlighted in this study may also become important targets for future research. They may be particularly useful for those studying whether the severity of a disease can be predicted, or when developing new therapies for serious infectious diseases. Although these findings are promising, they represent an important discovery stage rather than a clinical breakthrough. Before these genes can be used to identify children at risk of experiencing severe disease, they must be tested in larger groups of children

Low testosterone concentrations in hospitalized men correlate with elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly interleukin-6, and progressive testosterone decline accompanied by rising interleukin-10 levels tracks with increasing disease severity and death risk. Elevated estradiol-to-testosterone ratios, conversely, are associated with hyperinflammatory states and higher hospital mortality. Yet the molecular machinery through which sex steroids regulate immune and endothelial responses to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has remained only partially characterized. A new study published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology by Sandra Bižić-Radulović of the University Clinical Center of Serbia and colleagues now provides detailed mechanistic evidence that androgenic and estrogenic signaling exert opposing, cell-type-specific effects on virus-induced inflammatory pathways. The research team hypothesized that β-estradiol and dihydrotestosterone (DHT), the most potent androgen, would differentially modulate inflammatory signaling and monocyte–endothelial interactions during SARS-CoV-2 exposure. To test this, they exposed HULEC-5a lung microvascular endothelial cells, THP-1 monocytic leukemia cells, and primary monocytes and neutrophils isolated from patients with confirmed COVID-19 to in vitro-amplified Wuhan-1 SARS-CoV-2 at a multiplicity of infection of 0.001 for 24 and 48 hours. All procedures involving live virus were conducted in a certified Biosafety Level 3 laboratory in accordance with institutional biosafety regulations and World Health Organization recommendations. Cells were treated with DHT, β-estradiol, or the androgen receptor antagonist flutamide at nanomolar to micromolar concentrations before viral exposure. Receptor gene expression was measured by RT-qPCR, inflammatory signaling by Western blot against phosphorylated and total NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK proteins, and monocyte transendothelial migration by Boyden chamber assay. Patient samples were collected between June 2020 and April 2022 at the Clinic for Infectious and Tropical Diseases of the University Clinical Center of Serbia. The first key finding concerns how SARS-CoV-2 itself reshapes the expression of sex steroid receptors in a cell-specific manner. The virus reduced expression of estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1) in endothelial cells after 24 hours (p<0.05), while simultaneously increasing ESR1 expression in neutrophils (p<0.05) and monocytes (p<0.01) from patients with COVID-19. Androgen receptor (AR) expression was inversely regulated in neutrophils and monocytes: the virus reduced AR in neutrophils after 24 hours (p<0.001) but increased it in monocytes (p<0.05). These differential patterns suggest that SARS-CoV-2 actively reprograms the hormonal responsiveness of both vascular and immune compartments. The authors propose that suppression of ESR1 in endothelial cells may contribute to endothelial dysfunction, vascular inflammation, and thrombotic complications of severe disease, whereas increased ESR1 in circulating innate immune cells may represent a compensatory immunoregulatory response to systemic inflammation. In THP-1 monocytic cells, SARS-CoV-2 generally activated inflammatory signaling pathways including NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK, with activation reaching up to 1.9-fold above baseline. The NFκB response was further augmented by DHT (44.6%) and attenuated by flutamide (44.1%), indicating that androgen receptor signaling amplifies a central mediator of virus-induced cytokine production. STAT3 signaling was also activated by the virus (p<0.01), and both AR activation and AR blockade were associated with sustained STAT3 phosphorylation at 48 hours, though with different temporal dynamics: the DHT-associated increase at 48 hours was 3.4-fold lower than at 24 hours, whereas the flutamide-associated level remained unchanged between the two time points. Prolonged p38 MAPK activation was maintained by a low dose of DHT (10 nM) and reduced by low-dose flutamide (100 nM), but not by higher flutamide concentrations, suggesting dose-dependent and pathway-specific modulation of inflammatory cascades by androgen-responsive mechanisms. In HULEC-5a lung endothelial cells of human male origin, the picture was notably different. SARS-CoV-2 reduced STAT3 activation at 24 hours (p<0.05), an effect not further modified by DHT or flutamide. After 48 hours, DHT alone reduced STAT3 activation even in the absence of virus (p<0.01), indicating a direct effect of androgen signaling on baseline STAT3 activity in endothelial cells. In SARS-CoV-2-exposed cells, DHT twice reduced virus-induced activation of the p38 MAPK pathway (p<0.05). These results suggest that androgen signaling can partially suppress inflammatory signaling in endothelial cells both at baseline and during viral exposure, a finding that contrasts with the amplifying effects observed in monocytic cells and underscores the highly cell-specific nature of sex steroid immunoregulation during SARS-CoV-2 infection. Primary immune cells from patients with COVID-19 revealed further complexity. In neutrophils, β-estradiol inhibited NFκB signaling 2.2-fold, whereas DHT stimulated it 4.9-fold. SARS-CoV-2 reduced NFκB activation in neutrophils from female patients after 24 hours (p<0.001), and β-estradiol further reduced NFκB activation in a dose-dependent manner irrespective of viral exposure (p<0.01). In contrast, DHT increased NFκB activation after 48 hours independently of SARS-CoV-2. Simultaneously, the virus strongly induced p38 MAPK activation in neutrophils (>10-fold) after 24 hours (p<0.001). The authors note that persistent p38 MAPK activation may sustain neutrophil activation despite partial NFκB inhibition, contributing to oxidative stress, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, and tissue damage associated with severe disease. They also highlight that G protein-coupled estrogen receptor 1 (GPER1), a membrane-associated estrogen receptor expressed in human monocytes and neutrophils, may regulate neutrophil inflammatory responses through cAMP/PKA/CREB and MAPK signaling pathways. In monocytes from patients with COVID-19, DHT at 1 nM enhanced NFκB activation in the presence of SARS-CoV-2 after 24 hours (p<0.05), while β-estradiol at 100 nM increased p38 MAPK activation (p<0.01) and at the lowest concentration tested (1 nM) increased p38 MAPK activation irrespective of viral exposure (p<0.05). Comparison of exposure durations showed stronger SARS-CoV-2-induced activation of NFκB and p38 MAPK after 24 hours than after 48 hours (p<0.05), indicating a transient but pronounced activation of these pathways during early viral exposure. Notably, SARS-CoV-2 activation of inflammatory signaling deteriorates over time in monocytes from patients with COVID-19 (p<0.05), suggesting that androgen-mediated amplification of NFκB and MAPK cascades may contribute to exaggerated innate immune activation and heightened inflammatory responses in male patients with severe disease. Perhaps the most functionally significant results emerged from the Boyden chamber migration assay. DHT significantly increased trans-endothelial migration of monocytes from patients with COVID-19 (p<0.001) and promoted detachment of SARS-CoV-2-exposed HULEC-5a endothelial cells (p<0.01). Monocyte migration through SARS-CoV-2-exposed endothelial layers was predominantly enhanced by DHT and, to a lesser extent, by β-estradiol and flutamide (p<0.001). After correction for endothelial background fluorescence and monocyte-only controls, increased migration remained evident, particularly in DHT-treated conditions. These findings suggest that androgen signaling promotes endothelial dysfunction and facilitates monocyte transmigration during SARS-CoV-2 infection, key events in COVID-19-associated immunothrombosis and vascular injury. Enhanced leukocyte trafficking across the endothelial barrier may promote tissue infiltration by inflammatory cells and aggravate local cytokine production. The authors acknowledge limitations, including that sex-stratified analyses were not uniformly performed across all experiments involving primary immune cells because of limited availability of freshly isolated samples, and that the use of HULEC-5a cells derived from a single male donor restricts assessment of sex-dependent differences in endothelial responses. Nevertheless, the findings elucidate molecular mechanisms driving male-biased COVID-19 severity and underscore the potential of targeting androgen-responsive pathways as a therapeutic strategy to mitigate severe viral inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Beyond SARS-CoV-2, the differential regulation of NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK pathways observed here may reflect fundamental mechanisms of sex hormone-mediated immunoregulation that extend to other immune-mediated and vascular diseases in which sex steroids contribute to disease susceptibility and progression. The study’s experimental design merits closer attention because it bridges two levels of analysis that are often treated separately in COVID-19 research: controlled cell-line experiments and primary cells drawn from acutely ill patients. By using the same Wuhan-1 viral stock, verified by sequencing and titrated by TCID50 and plaque assay, for every condition, the investigators minimized viral preparation as a confounding variable. The low multiplicity of infection of 0.001 is notable, as it means relatively few cells received productive viral input, yet robust signaling changes were still detectable. This suggests that even limited viral exposure can trigger substantial inflammatory pathway activation, consistent with the idea that a small number of infected cells can amplify responses through paracrine signaling, although the study did not directly test such amplification mechanisms. The choice of signaling readouts also connects the findings to established COVID-19 biology. NFκB is the canonical transcription factor driving transcription of tumor necrosis factor, interleukin-6, and interleukin-1 family cytokines, all of which are elevated in severe disease and correlate with the testosterone deficits described in the clinical literature. STAT3 links cytokine signaling, particularly through the interleukin-6 receptor JAK-STAT axis, to cell survival and inflammatory differentiation programs in monocytes and neutrophils. p38 MAPK is a stress-activated kinase implicated in cytokine translation, oxidative burst, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation. The observation that SARS-CoV-2 activated all three pathways in monocytic cells, and that androgen receptor agonism and antagonism shifted the magnitude of these responses in opposite directions, provides a mechanistic scaffold for interpreting why male patients with lower testosterone might nonetheless experience androgen-driven hyperinflammation, since DHT effects were observed at concentrations within the physiological range. The dose-dependence of the androgen effects deserves particular emphasis. In the THP-1 experiments, low-dose DHT at 10 nanomolar sustained p38 MAPK activation while low-dose flutamide at 100 nanomolar reduced it, but higher flutamide concentrations did not reproduce this effect. Such non-monotonic dose relationships are a recognized feature of sex steroid biology, where receptor occupancy, receptor isoform expression, and co-regulator availability can produce qualitatively different outcomes at different ligand concentrations. For translational purposes, this complexity cautions against simple assumptions that androgen blockade will uniformly suppress inflammatory signaling across all cell types and doses, and it highlights the need for careful pharmacological characterization before any therapeutic repurposing of androgen receptor antagonists in viral disease. The cell-type specificity of the findings is equally important. DHT amplified NFκB signaling in monocytic cells and neutrophils, yet it twice reduced virus-induced p38 MAPK activation in endothelial cells and lowered baseline STAT3 activity after 48 hours. This divergence means that androgen signaling cannot be characterized as simply pro- or anti-inflammatory; rather, its net effect on systemic inflammation depends on the relative contribution of vascular versus immune compartments to a given clinical phenotype. In severe COVID-19, where both endothelial injury and myeloid cell hyperactivation drive pathology, the opposing effects could partially offset each other or, alternatively, the monocyte- and neutrophil-directed amplification may dominate because these cells produce the circulating cytokines and tissue-damaging mediators observed in patients. The transendothelial migration results add a functional dimension that goes beyond signaling biochemistry. Monocyte recruitment across the endothelial barrier is a hallmark of vascular inflammation and contributes directly to immunothrombosis, the process by which leukocyte activation, tissue factor expression, and platelet engagement generate thrombi in the pulmonary and systemic microvasculature. The finding that DHT promoted monocyte migration with high statistical significance, and that it also induced detachment of virus-exposed endothelial cells, links androgen signaling to two mechanistically connected events: weakening of the endothelial monolayer and enhanced leukocyte trafficking through it. Detachment of endothelial cells, if it occurs in vivo, could expose subendothelial matrix and tissue factor, providing a procoagulant surface that complements the inflammatory effects of infiltrating monocytes. The differential regulation of estrogen receptor expression by the virus itself adds another layer of interpretation. Reduced ESR1 in endothelial cells could diminish the protective, anti-inflammatory tone that estrogen signaling normally provides to the vasculature, including nitric oxide-mediated vasodilation and suppression of adhesion molecule expression. Increased ESR1 in neutrophils and monocytes, conversely, might represent a compensatory attempt by innate immune cells to enhance estrogen-dependent immunoregulation during systemic inflammation. Whether this compensatory upregulation is functionally effective in patients, or is overwhelmed by the concurrent androgen-driven amplification of NFκB and MAPK signaling, remains an open question that would require measuring receptor protein levels and downstream estrogen-responsive gene expression in patient cells. The temporal dimension of the findings, with stronger pathway activation at 24 hours than at 48 hours in patient monocytes and progressive deterioration of inflammatory signaling over the course of disease, aligns with clinical observations that COVID-19 inflammation evolves in phases. Early innate immune activation, followed by sustained or dysregulated myeloid responses, characterizes progression toward severe disease. The observation that signaling responses in patient monocytes worsened over time suggests that longitudinal sampling, rather than single time-point measurements, may be necessary to capture the full trajectory of sex steroid modulation in COVID-19, and it raises the possibility that therapeutic timing, whether targeting androgen signaling early or late in disease, could substantially influence outcomes. Finally, the study’s reliance on the Wuhan-1 variant, collected during the first years of the pandemic, invites consideration of how these mechanisms might apply to later variants with altered inflammatory profiles. The core signaling pathways investigated here, NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK, are activated by multiple pattern recognition receptors and cytokine circuits, so the sex steroid modulation described is unlikely to be variant-specific in principle. However, the magnitude of viral replication, the efficiency of cell entry, and the specific cytokine milieu induced by different variants could shift the balance between androgen-amplified and estrogen-attenuated responses. Extending this experimental framework to contemporary variants, and to cells from vaccinated individuals with pre-existing adaptive immunity, would help determine whether the androgen-responsive mechanisms identified here remain relevant targets for mitigating severe viral inflammation and endothelial dysfunction in current clinical practice. records.content: PITTSBORO — Updated flu and COVID-19 vaccines are now available through the Chatham County Public Health Department as health officials encourage residents to protect themselves ahead of the fall and winter respiratory virus season. The vaccines are being offered at the department's Siler City clinic. Residents can schedule appointments by calling 919-742-5641. Flu shots are available at no cost for children and adults, while COVID-19 vaccines are available at no cost to eligible children through the Vaccines for Children Program. Insurance providers will be billed for patients with coverage. Vaccines also are available at pharmacies and other health care providers throughout the county. The announcement comes as respiratory virus activity begins to increase across North Carolina. On Oct. 8, the N.C. Department of Health and Human Services announced the state's first reported flu-related death of the 2026-27 season. During the 2025-26 flu season, North Carolina recorded 338 flu-related deaths, including nine children. "Getting vaccinated is one of the best ways to protect yourself and your loved ones, especially during the colder months when respiratory viruses are on the rise," said Chatham County Public Health Director Mike Zelek. "By getting an updated vaccine for the season, you're helping protect your health and the health of those around you as we head into fall and winter." Health officials also encourage residents to practice preventive measures to limit the spread of influenza, COVID-19 and other respiratory illnesses. Those precautions include frequent handwashing with soap and water, regularly cleaning frequently touched surfaces such as doorknobs and countertops, and staying home when experiencing symptoms such as coughing, fever or a sore throat. Residents seeking vaccinations can contact their health care provider, local pharmacy or the Chatham County Public Health Department. For more information about seasonal flu and COVID-19, visit www.chathamcountync.gov/flu or www.chathamcountync.gov/covid . Additional information about the Chatham County Public Health Department is available at www.chathamcountync.gov/publichealth . Juss.,楝科)因其广泛的药理活性而备受科学关注,包括抗病毒、抗菌、抗癌、抗氧化、抗炎和免疫调节特性。印楝的治疗潜力主要与其所含的柠檬苦素类化合物有关,这是一类高度氧化的四降三萜类化合物。已有研究表明,印楝中的多种柠檬苦素类化合物对登革病毒、基孔肯雅病毒和SARS-CoV-2相关分子靶点显示出抗病毒活性。 在此背景下,本研究旨在通过整合计算机模拟策略,包括药效团建模、杂合配体设计、分子对接和ADMET预测,识别和表征源自印楝柠檬苦素类化合物的潜在SARS-CoV-2 Mpro抑制剂。此外,研究还试图探究抗病毒柠檬苦素的结构杂交是否能增强其与Mpro催化位点和别构位点的分子间相互作用,从而为发现具有潜在可接受药代动力学特性的新型抗病毒候选物做出贡献。 研究方法概述 研究人员首先通过文献检索筛选了三种具有抗病毒活性的印楝柠檬苦素类化合物(7-Deacetyl-7-benzoylgedunin、Gedunin和Azadirone)。利用MOE软件进行柔性叠合和药效团建模,识别共同药效特征并设计杂合分子Limotest。采用AutoDock 4.2软件,将Limotest与Mpro(PDB ID: 7K40)的催化位点、别构位点I(AS I)、别构位点II(AS II)以及预结合底物的催化位点进行分子对接,并以恩赛特韦(ensitrelvir)作为参照药物。通过ADMETlab 3.0和ProTox 3.0平台预测Limotest的药代动力学和毒性特性。 研究结果 3.1 抗病毒植物化学物质的筛选 研究人员从印楝中约130种柠檬苦素类三萜化合物中,基于文献报道的抗病毒活性证据,选择了三种化合物用于药效团建模。 3.2 柔性叠合、药效团搜索与杂合配体设计 通过MOE软件的柔性叠合分析,三种化合物显示出若干几何相似性。基于叠合结果,研究人员鉴定了氢键受体投影(Acc2)、氢键受体(Acc)、疏水中心(Hyd)、芳香中心(Aro)和芳环/正常Pi环(PiN)等药效团特征。最终,基于这三种柠檬苦素的共同结构特征设计了一个杂合分子,命名为Limotest。 3.3 药代动力学参数预测 ADMET预测结果显示,Limotest的人肠道吸收率(HIA)大于30%;稳态分布容积(VDss)低于0.7 L/kg,提示其倾向于集中在血浆中;血脑屏障(BBB)通透性低;血浆蛋白结合率(PPB)为94.559%。在代谢方面,Limotest是CYP1A2、CYP2C19、CYP2C9和CYP3A4的底物,但对多数CYP酶抑制作用低,不过对CYP2B6和CYP2C8有潜在抑制作用。毒性预测显示,Limotest半数致死剂量(LD50)高达12,300 mg/kg,属于毒性等级6级,对肝毒性、神经毒性、致癌性、致突变性和细胞毒性呈阴性,但对肾毒性、心脏毒性和免疫毒性呈阳性。 3.4 抗SARS-CoV-2活性预测 分子对接协议验证显示重对接的均方根偏差(RMSD)值在可接受范围内。Limotest在催化位点的结合能在-11.21至-11.06 kcal/mol之间,在不同对接方案下结合姿势无显著变化,形成了两个氢键(与Gly 143和Arg 188)、两个碳氢键(与Phe 140和Asn 142)、一个Pi-硫相互作用(与Cys 145)、一个Pi-σ相互作用(与His 41)和一个Pi-烷基相互作用(与Leu 27)。参照药物恩赛特韦的结合能为-6.94 kcal/mol。当Mpro预结合底物后,Limotest的结合能从-11.21 kcal/mol升至-7.56 kcal/mol,且定位于催化位点外部。在AS I,Limotest获得了最高的结合能-12.91 kcal/mol,形成四个氢键(与Arg 4A、Arg 4B、Lys B5和Trp 207A)及六个烷基/Pi-烷基相互作用。在AS II,Limotest的结合能为-9.71 kcal/mol,形成两个氢键(与Lys 12A和Lys 12B)。 讨论与结论总结 讨论部分指出,本研究的药效团模型应被视为探索性框架而非完全验证的预测模型。Limotest在催化位点的稳定结合模式表明其在Mpro的非活性(单体)和活性(二聚体)形式下均能维持一致的结合方式。在底物存在时,Limotest的结合亲和力下降并定位到活性口袋外部,这提示其具有底物模拟特性,可能与Mpro的天然底物竞争,表明其潜在的竞争性抑制机制。值得注意的是,Limotest在AS I获得了最优异的对接评分,这可能是一个关键的抑制位点。 研究结论部分翻译如下:本研究评估了设计的杂合柠檬苦素化合物Limotest与SARS-CoV-2 Mpro的相互作用。分子对接分析显示了有利的相互作用谱,表明Limotest可能是一种有前景的未来抗病毒研究计算候选物。Limotest对SARS-CoV-2 Mpro表现出良好的计算相互作用谱,可能是有待未来实验验证的有前景候选物。虽然其结合姿势在与底物叠加时基本保持不变,但观察到了结合能的位移,提示底物模拟性以及对底物可及的别构位点I更强的亲和力。该化合物的ADMET谱也得到了评估,显示出良好的药代动力学和毒理学特性。基于这些发现,Limotest可能通过竞争性抑制机制,与Mpro活性位点的天然底物竞争。然而,仍需进一步的实验验证来确认其作为抗病毒药物的效力。此外,先前报道的印楝柠檬苦素的抗病毒活性进一步支持了这些化合物作为未来抗SARS-CoV-2筛选和实验验证的有前景候选物的相关性。 records.content: skip to main content The Magazine STORIES THAT MATTER LoginRegister Stay Curious Search Subscribe The Sciences Mind Technology Health Environment Planet Earth STORIES THAT MATTER Subscribe The Sciences COVID-19 Variants This Fall, Gray Wolves Use Wildfires to Hunt, and a Blood Test Could Detect Breast Cancer Discover the top stories from Oct. 10 to Oct. 16, 2026, including what COVID-19 variants scientists are currently tracking and how gray wolves are using active wildfires to hunt. Written byStephanie Edwards Stephanie Edwards Stephanie Edwards is the Engagement Specialist at Discover Magazine, who manages all social media platforms and writes digital articles that focus on archaeology, the environment, and public health. View Full Profile. Learn about our Editorial Policy. Oct 16, 2026, 7:36 PM | 2 min read (Image Credit: Shutterstock: fikretow; Kjetil Kolbjornsrud; Frame Stock Footage; antoniodiaz; Adam_photos) Newsletter Sign up for our email newsletter for the latest science news Sign Up Did you catch the top stories this week? Check out our roundup below, covering the biggest science news and stories that matter. This week's stories, from Oct. 10 to Oct. 16, 2026, include an uptick in COVID-19 variants, how the Nordic diet could extend your lifespan, gray wolves may be using wildfire to pursue prey, a new look at the body development of Homo sapiens, the start of clinical trials for a breast cancer blood test, and how drones helped find three new Aboriginal rock shelters in Australia. 1. COVID-19 Cases Are Picking Up Again — These Are the Variants That Health Officials Are Watching COVID-19 variant (Image Credit: fikretow/Shutterstock) As we near infectious disease season, increased rates of common respiratory illnesses are already taking hold. Viruses that cause COVID-19, the flu, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) change their genetic makeup between seasons, confronting health authorities with new changes at the start of each winter season. Read More: COVID-19 Cases Are Picking Up Again — These Are the Variants That Health Officials Are Watching 2. Nordic Diet May Help Extend Your Lifespan by Adding Whole Grains and Berries to Your Plate The Mediterranean diet has grown immensely popular for its emphasis on plant-based foods and olive oil, but another regional diet with roots in Europe may bring its own benefits to the table. The Nordic diet, based on foods commonly eaten across the Nordic countries, provides its own spin on healthy eating by promoting whole grains, berries, and rapeseed oil. You have 1 more free article (1 of 2) Have an account? log in Subscribe today for full access and support our journalism. Explore All Options Read More: Nordic Diet May Help Extend Your Lifespan by Adding Whole Grains and Berries to Your Plate 3. Gray Wolves May Use Active Wildfires to Pursue Prey While Avoiding Dangerous Fire Fronts (Image Credit: Kjetil Kolbjornsrud/Shutterstock) Wildfires are becoming more and more common. They burn through wild areas, forcing many of the animals that live there to flee. There is one animal, however, that may have found a way to use these fires to their advantage: The gray wolf. Read More: Gray Wolves May Use Active Wildfires to Pursue Prey While Avoiding Dangerous Fire Fronts 4. A 230,000-Year-Old Homo sapiens Fossil Reveals Early Humans Were More Robust Than Once Thought When Omo I lived, more than 230,000 years ago, her skull already displayed features characteristic of Homo sapiens, including a high, rounded cranial vault and a chin. But her body may still have been very different from the one we associate with our species. Read More: A 230,000-Year-Old Homo sapiens Fossil Reveals Early Humans Were More Robust Than Once Thought 5. A Blood Test That Could Detect Breast Cancer as Early as Stage I Has Started Clinical Trials Researchers at USC Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center, part of Keck Medicine of USC, are investigating whether a blood test could help clarify breast cancer findings sooner. A new clinical trial will evaluate whether the blood test can work alongside mammograms to detect breast cancer as early as Stage I. Read More: A Blood Test That Could Detect Breast Cancer as Early as Stage I Has Started Clinical Trials 6. Drones Help Find Three Aboriginal Rock Shelters With Red Hand Stencils After drones flagged possible rock shelters in Australia’s Blue Mountains, archaeologist Amy Mosig Way led students and volunteers into the bush to check the locations on foot. Inside, stone artifacts and red hand stencils preserved evidence of past Aboriginal life, connecting the places they were recording with the people who had used them generations before. [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7]。特别是CRISPR-Cas系统结合等温核酸扩增技术,实现了与PCR相当的特异性和灵敏度,而且检测时间不到1小时,并可在现场(POC)使用[8], [9], [10]。其中一些方法获得了美国食品药品监督管理局(FDA)的紧急使用授权(例如SHERLOCK CRISPR SARS-CoV-2试剂盒[11])。然而,为了进一步提高CRISPR基分子诊断方法的效果,还需在减少检测时间、提高灵敏度和简化操作流程方面进行更多创新。 CRISPR-Cas12a(旧称Cpf1)是一种V型系统,已被用于检测SARS-CoV-2、其他病原体[2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [12], [13], [14], [15],甚至哺乳动物细胞系中的基因突变[16]。它通过Cas12a蛋白与CRISPR RNA(crRNA)之间的相互作用形成核蛋白复合物(RNP),其中crRNA由重复序列(20个核苷酸)和可变序列(20-24个核苷酸)组成[17], [18]。crRNA可以被编程以特异性地检测互补的目标DNA序列,前提是这些序列位于PAM序列(TTTV)的3'端。识别到目标序列后,Cas12a会激活其核酸酶RuvC结构域,切割双链DNA。RuvC结构域持续活跃,还能切割单链DNA报告探针(即所谓的“跨切割”活性或附带活性),从而产生可检测的比色或荧光信号。 尽管CRISPR-Cas12a系统的检测限(LoD)据报道在皮摩尔(pM)范围内[13],但根据酶-靶标对的催化效率模型,其LoD不可能低于100飞摩尔(fM)[19]。因此,单靠CRISPR-Cas12a难以检测到临床实际意义的SARS-CoV-2量[20]。环介导等温扩增(LAMP)[21], [22]可以在几分钟内指数级放大目标序列的数量,从而将CRISPR-Cas的检测灵敏度提高数个数量级[23], [24]。然而,LAMP需要在60至65°C的温度下运行,而CRISPR-Cas系统通常在37°C下进行,这导致需要使用两种不同的温度。消除这种温差限制将带来显著优势:它可以简化实验流程、减少所需设备数量和孵育步骤、加快检测速度、缩短获取结果的时间,甚至可能使LAMP和CRISPR-Cas反应并行进行。因此,找到一种简单的方法来解决这一温度限制问题,将对改进基于CRISPR的分子诊断方法的发展产生积极影响。 温度是影响酶活性和动力学的关键参数,直接关系到基于CRISPR的方法的准确性、效率、实用性、特异性和灵敏度。调整Cas蛋白工作的温度具有挑战性,因为它们通常只在较窄的温度范围内表现出最佳活性。本研究中使用的Cas12a的同源蛋白AsCas12a(来源于Acidaminococcus sp)被认为是非热稳定的。据报道,AsCas12a的熔解温度(Tm)约为40°C,与crRNA结合后升至约49°C或约54°C[25], [26]。其他常用的CRISPR诊断蛋白如LwaCas13a也是如此,其单体形式的Tm为45°C[27]。 为了解决温度不兼容的问题,研究小组寻找了Cas12a蛋白的热稳定同源蛋白[25], [27], [28]或设计了热稳定蛋白版本[29]。通过基因数据库筛选,发现了热稳定的Cme和YmeCas12a,它们的单体形式Tm分别为55°C和56°C,形成RNP后Tm分别升至61°C和65°C[25]。此外,一系列名为“SLK”的Cas12a同源蛋白的RNP Tm介于43°C至65°C之间[27]。还有报道指出,AacCas12b和AapCas12b的RNP Tm分别为56°C和63.4°C[30], [31]。Nguyen等人于2023年利用机器学习技术创建了一种高度热稳定的Cas12b蛋白版本,实现了CRISPR-Cas和RT-LAMP的联合应用[29]。不过,这些方法虽然有效,但需要大量资源和时间来寻找适用于所需温度的热稳定同源蛋白或对蛋白质进行精细工程改造。如果能找到更简单的方法,让CRISPR-Cas检测在更高温度下使用已知且特性明确的系统进行,将对CRISPR诊断领域带来很大帮助。 在本研究中,我们旨在探索野生型(wt)AsCas12a蛋白在高温下特异性检测DNA的条件,并利用这些条件来提高SARS-CoV-2的检测效果(见图1)。我们首先研究了孵育温度(高达65°C)对DNA检测速度的影响。出乎意料的是,我们发现CRISPR-AsCas12a在65°C下仍能检测到编码SARS-CoV-2 N基因的DNA(见图1B),速度比在30°C快8倍,比在37°C快3倍,且没有产生假阳性结果。在优化了65°C下的缓冲条件后,检测速度进一步提高了1.6倍(见图1C)。最终,通过结合最佳温度和缓冲条件,我们建立了一种使用荧光和侧向流动条检测SARS-CoV-2的两步方法,并证明了该方法能够区分Omicron变异株和野生型株(见图1D)。该流程通过临床样本验证,检测时间缩短至不到10分钟。这证明了无需改造热稳定蛋白版本,就能通过温度优化提升野生型CRISPR-AsCas12a的性能和速度,从而改进病原体检测。 章节片段 材料 醋酸钾、醋酸镁、NaCl、(NH4)2SO4、MnSO4、MgCl2、DTT、BSA、亚精胺、Triton?X-100、KCl、PEG-8000和L-脯氨酸均购自Sigma-Aldrich(美国马萨诸塞州伯灵顿);tris、甘氨酸和 Tween 20购自Bio-Rad(美国加利福尼亚州赫拉克勒斯);HCl和醋酸钠分别购自JT Baker(美国宾夕法尼亚州拉德诺)和Affymetrix-USB(美国加利福尼亚州圣克拉拉)。所有材料均为分析级质量。 crRNA和引物的合成 所有RT-LAMP引物、crRNA和报告探针均由我们自行合成。 高温对CRISPR-AsCas12a检测DNA的影响 首先,我们研究了温度对检测携带SARS-CoV-2核衣壳(N)基因的pDNA的RNP附带活性的影响(见图1)。我们假设,在高于报道的Tm(约45-50°C)[25], [26]的温度下孵育AsCas12a会对DNA检测产生负面影响。有两种可能的结果:(i)由于蛋白质变性,附带活性显著降低;(ii)附带活性完全消失。 结论 将CRISPR-AsCas12a反应温度升高至65°C后,附带切割活性得到增强,而不影响其稳定性,从而实现了更快速和特异的核酸检测。通过系统化的缓冲液优化,荧光信号强度提高了三倍,检测时间减少到了约7分钟。 伦理批准 本研究中未涉及任何人类和/或动物。 资金来源 本研究得到了UNAM-PAPIIT(IV200820)的支持。 未引用的参考文献 [45] Mario Alanis records.content_title: Poor Glycemic Control Associated With Cytokine Storm & Severe COVID-19 Outcomes | Physicians Weekly
records.content: Among hospitalized patients with COVID-19, diabetes and hyperglycemia remain important markers of disease severity and mortality risk. However, a recent retrospective analysis published in Frontiers in Clinical Diabetes and Healthcare suggests that obesity may be associated with a survival advantage, adding to the ongoing debate surrounding the so-called “obesity paradox.” Poor Glycemic Control Associated With Cytokine Storm & Severe COVID-19 Outcomes Diabetes, Hyperglycemia, & Cytokine Storm Signal Greater Risk Researchers evaluated 478 adults hospitalized with COVID-19 at an urban academic medical center in Philadelphia from March to May 2020, examining how diabetes, glycemic control, BMI, and inflammatory complications such as cytokine storm influenced clinical outcomes. Preexisting diabetes was present in 36% of patients, with most cases representing type 2 diabetes. Compared with patients without diabetes, those with diabetes were significantly older and more likely to require mechanical ventilation (8.7% versus 2.6%; P<0.001). Hyperglycemia occurred in 73.4% of patients with diabetes versus 11.5% of those without diabetes. Beyond traditional markers of disease severity, the researchers found a significant relationship between glycemic control and cytokine storm. Among patients with available HbA1c data, those who developed cytokine storm had significantly higher mean HbA1c levels than those who did not. The finding is significant given that cytokine storm affected 14% of hospitalized patients and was associated with nearly a threefold increase in mortality (30.8% versus 11.4%; P<0.001), suggesting that chronic hyperglycemia may contribute to the exaggerated inflammatory response observed in severe COVID-19. Mortality was also higher among patients with diabetes, hypertension, hyperglycemia, and steroid-induced hyperglycemia. Among patients requiring ICU care, rates of hyperglycemia and steroid-induced hyperglycemia (61.3% and 21.5%, respectively) were markedly elevated compared with those who did not require critical care (26.5% versus 3.9%; P<0.0001). In multivariable analyses, steroid-induced hyperglycemia and obstructive sleep apnea emerged as independent predictors of ICU admission. Higher BMI Associated With Improved Survival Nearly three-quarters of the cohort were either overweight (29%) or obese (45%). However, deceased patients had a significantly lower mean BMI than survivors (28.1 kg/m2 versus 31.0 kg/m2; P=0.006). Kaplan-Meier analyses showed improved survival among patients who were overweight and obese compared with those of normal weight. Importantly, BMI remained significantly associated with mortality after adjustment for age, sex, race, smoking status, and diabetes status (P=0.006). The authors noted that these findings may reflect an obesity paradox, a phenomenon previously reported in conditions such as heart failure and sepsis. They also cautioned that selection bias, differences in clinical management, and the limitations of BMI as a marker of body composition may partially explain the observed relationship. The findings reinforce the importance of aggressive monitoring and management of dysglycemia in hospitalized patients with COVID-19. In addition to increasing the risk for severe clinical outcomes, poor long-term glycemic control was associated with cytokine storm, highlighting the potential role of metabolic health in inflammatory responses. Although higher BMI was linked to improved survival in this cohort, further studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms underlying the obesity paradox and determine whether these findings are generalizable to broader patient populations. Clinical Implications - Patients with diabetes and hyperglycemia face increased risks for severe COVID-19 outcomes, including ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and death. - Elevated HbA1c levels were associated with cytokine storm, underscoring the importance of maintaining glycemic control and closely monitoring inflammatory complications. - Although patients who were overweight and obese demonstrated improved survival in this cohort, BMI should be interpreted alongside overall metabolic health and other clinical risk factors. References Sadiq S, et al. Front Clin Diabetes Healthc. 2026;7:1946918. doi:10.3389/fcdhc.2026.1946918

controls),研究发现超过三分之一的阳性检测结果增长无法由县区层面的人口、经济、医疗保健或儿童保育特征,也无法由距离伊施格尔(Ischgl)的距离——一个与德国第一波COVID-19疫情相关的滑雪旅游代理变量——所解释。在巴伐利亚内部,控制了诸如距离伊施格尔的距离和烈性啤酒节数量等替代驱动因素后,选民参与率较高的县区在选举后经历了更陡峭的COVID-19病例和死亡人数增长。研究结果高度稳健,表明不幸的选举时间安排助长了传染病的传播。 一、研究背景与研究动机 欢迎领取《类器官应用方案 3D之旅》领 取 2020年初,COVID-19疫情迅速席卷全球,各国政府面临如何在保障公民健康权与维护民主政治权利之间取得平衡的严峻挑战。许多国家选择推迟全国性或地方性选举,或转向邮寄投票。然而,德国巴伐利亚州于2020年3月15日如期举行了地区选举,当时仅有少数预防措施到位,佩戴口罩甚至被官方劝阻以节省医用物资。这一决策为研究人员提供了一个独特的准自然实验情境,用以评估大规模人群聚集活动——尤其是选举——在缺乏有效防护措施的条件下对传染病传播的真实影响。 此前已有研究探讨了美国大学春假、特朗普竞选集会、意大利地区选举、法国市镇选举及威斯康星州初选等事件对COVID-19传播的影响,但结论并不一致。部分研究发现了显著的正向关联,另一些则未观察到明显效应。这些矛盾的结果凸显了跨情境验证的必要性。巴伐利亚选举的特殊之处在于其发生在疫情初期、公众认知有限且防护措施严重不足的时间节点,这使其成为检验选举作为病毒传播放大器机制的理想案例。此外,相较于其他研究中可能存在的选民自我选择偏差(如高风险群体因恐惧而回避投票),巴伐利亚的选民参与率反而较上一届有所上升,且在已报告确诊病例的县区并未出现明显的参与率下降,这有助于缓解内生性问题。 因此,研究人员旨在通过严谨的因果推断方法,量化巴伐利亚地区选举对后续COVID-19病例和死亡人数增长的贡献,从而为未来公共卫生危机中的选举安排提供实证依据。 二、研究方法概述 研究人员采用两种互补的计量经济学方法进行因果识别。 第一种方法是合成控制法(Synthetic Control Method, SCM)。该方法为巴伐利亚州的96个县区逐一构建了一个合成的反事实对照组。合成对照组的权重来自全德范围内非巴伐利亚的县区(即“捐赠池”),权重分配依据是县区层面的一系列预测变量,包括人口结构、经济状况、医疗保健和儿童保育特征,以及到奥地利滑雪胜地伊施格尔(Ischgl)的驾车时间——后者被用作早期疫情输入风险的代理变量。研究人员排除了举办过烈性啤酒节的县区以避免混淆效应,最终纳入87个处理单元。通过比较实际观测到的疫情发展轨迹与合成反事实之间的差异,研究人员估计出选举的平均处理效应(ATT)。 第二种方法是巴伐利亚州内的截面回归分析。研究人员将选举后(3月15日至4月5日)各县区每10万居民中COVID-19病例和死亡人数的增量作为因变量,以选民参与率(%)作为核心解释变量,同时控制选举前两周的疫情基线水平、居家办公比例、到伊施格尔的距离、烈性啤酒节数量以及行政和结构性县区类型虚拟变量。该模型采用普通最小二乘法(OLS)估计,并使用怀特异方差稳健标准误。 三、研究结果 1. 合成控制法结果: 研究人员发现,平均而言,巴伐利亚各县区的合成对照组在选举前与真实数据拟合良好(RMSPE=0.007)。从选举后一周开始,真实巴伐利亚县区与合成对照组之间的病例数差距逐渐扩大。到日历周13(选举后约两周),真实巴伐利亚县区的每周新增病例数比合成对照组高出约每10万人20例,这意味着超过三分之一的病例增长无法由县区层面的可观测特征或滑雪旅游因素解释。安慰剂检验(将其他州县区伪设为处理组)显示,巴伐利亚观察到的效应在统计上显著(调整后p值较低),且RMSPE比值分布也支持这一结论。对于COVID-19相关死亡,由于选举前死亡基数极低,合成控制法的结果不够稳定,未能达到统计显著性。 2. 州内回归分析结果: 在控制了所有协变量的最保守模型中,选民参与率每增加1个百分点,与选举后三周内每10万居民中额外增加12.8例COVID-19病例和1.8例死亡相关联,两者均在统计上显著。即使进一步纳入烈性啤酒节数量作为控制变量,该效应依然稳健。研究人员还探索了时间动态,发现选举效应在选举后第二周开始显现,并在第三周达到峰值。当区分邮寄投票和现场投票时,两种方式均显示出与疫情传播的正向关联,但现场投票的效应略大。 四、讨论与结论 研究人员指出,尽管合成控制法和回归分析均强有力地表明巴伐利亚地区选举促进了COVID-19的传播,但这一结论并不意味着应取消民主选举,而是强调在疫情期间举行选举时需要采取充分的防护措施。该研究的独特价值在于其聚焦于疫情初期、公众认知和防护手段都极为有限的特殊时期,这与后来已经实施社交距离和口罩令的情境形成鲜明对比。研究结果的一般性启示在于,选举的时间安排——通常集中在春季或秋季——可能会加剧其他季节性传染病的传播,例如流感,这值得未来研究进一步探讨。 结论翻译: 研究结果强烈且稳健地表明,2020年3月15日的地区选举促进了COVID-19在巴伐利亚的传播。这些结果更一般性地暗示,选举在一年中的时间安排——通常发生在春季或秋季——可能会促进其他季节性传染病(如流感)的传播。研究人员将此问题留待未来研究。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! Rates: A Nationwide Time-to-Event Analysis During the COVID-19 Pandemic 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月17日 来源:Resuscitation Plus 3.1 编辑推荐: 背景:及时的旁观者心肺复苏(bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation, BCPR)对于院外心脏骤停(out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, OHCA)后的生存至关重要。尽管COVID-19疫情期间总 揭幕测序新体验,领取Twist Exome 2.0详细技术资料,助力您的表观遗传学研究 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 背景:及时的旁观者心肺复苏(bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation, BCPR)对于院外心脏骤停(out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, OHCA)后的生存至关重要。尽管COVID-19疫情期间总体BCPR启动率报道不一致,BCPR启动时机很少受到关注。本研究评估了目击OHCA后10分钟内BCPR的启动情况。 方法:这项回顾性队列研究使用了日本全国Utstein登记库(All-Japan Utstein registry)。纳入2019年和2020年3月11日至12月31日期间发生的成人非创伤性、非专业人员目击OHCA。主要结局是目击后10分钟内启动BCPR。采用Kaplan–Meier和Cox模型进行时间-事件分析。探索性logistic回归检验了BCPR启动时机与1个月结局之间的关联。 结果:在56,082例合格病例(疫情前27,770例;疫情期间28,312例)中,总体BCPR启动率保持稳定(58.7% vs. 58.6%,p = 0.759)。然而,时间-事件分析发现早期BCPR启动存在轻微差异(log-rank p = 0.010),疫情期间启动风险较低(调整后风险比[adjusted hazard ratio, aHR] 0.96;95%置信区间[confidence interval, CI] 0.93–0.98)。在接受BCPR的患者中,更早启动与1个月时更好的神经功能预后几率相关(0–3、4–7和8–10分钟分别调整后优势比[adjusted odds ratio, aOR] 3.27、2.66和1.68;参考组>10分钟)。在校正BCPR启动时机后,疫情期间仍与较低的1个月生存率相关(aOR 0.86;95% CI,0.80–0.92)。 结论:尽管疫情期间总体BCPR启动率未发生变化,时间-事件分析发现早期BCPR启动出现轻微下降。早期BCPR与更好的结局相关,但启动时机的差异并不能完全解释疫情期间较低的生存率。 院外心脏骤停(OHCA)是重大公共卫生问题,全球每年发病规模巨大,出院存活率平均约9%。及时启动旁观者心肺复苏(BCPR)是决定存活的关键环节。既往研究(Nguyen等、O'Keefe等)已证明,旁观者心肺复苏启动越晚,生存获益呈梯度下降,因此启动时机而非仅仅“是否实施”具有重要意义。然而常规BCPR质量指标多为二分类,只记录是否实施CPR,无法反映心脏骤停发生后最初10分钟这一关键时间窗内的启动时机差异。COVID-19疫情作为自然实验可能改变 bystander 行为与急救系统响应,但已有研究对总体BCPR率的影响报告不一致,且对启动时机关注有限。日本按疫情强度将13个都道府县划为特别警报区域(SAA),限制措施可能增加家庭内目击比例,而家人目击的BCPR率低于非家人目击。研究人员据此假设:疫情与早期BCPR启动概率降低相关,且这种差异能被时间-事件分析检出,但不表现为总体BCPR率的变化。 了解Twist为新冠病毒设计的合成RNA阳性对照>>领 取 研究人员利用日本全国Utstein登记库(All-Japan Utstein registry)开展回顾性队列研究,纳入2019年和2020年3月11日至12月31日成人非创伤性、非专业人员目击OHCA共56,082例,以目击后10分钟内启动BCPR为主要结局。结果发现,尽管总体BCPR率稳定,早期BCPR启动概率在疫情期间出现轻微下降;更早启动BCPR与更好的1个月生存和神经功能预后相关;但疫情相关的生存下降并不能完全由BCPR启动时机差异解释。该研究提示,在传统二分类指标之外补充“目击至BCPR启动时间”作为质量改进与登记报告的指标,能更敏感地发现早期旁观者干预的变化。 关键技术方法方面,研究基于覆盖日本47个都道府县、约1.255亿人口的全国前瞻性登记库,纳入成人非创伤性、非专业人员目击OHCA,排除EMS人员目击、关键时间变量缺失及超过60分钟的极端时间间隔。采用Kaplan–Meier法以目击时间为时间零点绘制BCPR启动累积概率曲线,并用log-rank检验比较疫情前后;Cox比例风险模型估计10分钟内BCPR启动风险,调整年龄、性别、目击者关系、调度员CPR指令;按SAA进行亚组及交互作用分析,并做敏感性分析。进一步采用多变量logistic回归分析BCPR启动时机(0–3、4–7、8–10、>10分钟)与1个月生存及神经功能预后的关联。 纳入病例与基线特征方面,共有56,082例符合条件,疫情前27,770例,疫情期间28,312例。疫情期间家人作为目击者的比例高于疫情前(61.8% vs. 59.8%,p < 0.001),调度员CPR指令提供比例也更高(60.3% vs. 57.8%,p < 0.001)。 总体BCPR率与早期启动的时间-事件分析方面,疫情前后总体BCPR启动率无显著差异(58.7% vs. 58.6%,p = 0.759),但时间-事件曲线显示,疫情期间最初数分钟内BCPR启动概率更低,10分钟内早期启动差异有统计学意义(log-rank p = 0.010),调整后风险比(aHR)为0.96(95% CI 0.93–0.98)。去除目击者关系和调度员CPR指令后的敏感性分析结果相似(aHR 0.97;95% CI 0.95–0.99)。 亚组分析方面,在特别警报区域(SAA),疫情期间早期BCPR启动风险显著降低(aHR 0.94;95% CI 0.91–0.96),非SAA无显著关联(aHR 0.99;95% CI 0.96–1.03),交互作用检验提示区域政策强度可能具有异质性(交互项HR 0.95;95% CI 0.91–0.99;P = 0.028)。 旁观者干预与临床结局方面,疫情期间单纯胸外按压CPR比例升高(85.3% vs. 87.7%),含人工呼吸的CPR比例下降(12.5% vs. 10.4%),旁观者AED使用比例下降(4.1% vs. 3.2%,p < 0.001)。自主循环恢复(ROSC)率(19.8% vs. 16.7%)、1个月生存率(11.4% vs. 9.4%)及1个月良好神经功能预后率(6.4% vs. 5.0%)均低于疫情前。 BCPR启动时机与1个月结局的关联方面,在接受BCPR的患者中,更早启动与更高的1个月生存和良好神经功能预后独立相关:与>10分钟相比,0–3、4–7、8–10分钟的良好神经功能预后aOR分别为3.27、2.66、1.68;1个月生存aOR分别为2.68、2.39、1.74。校正BCPR启动时机后,疫情期仍与较低的1个月生存率(aOR 0.86;95% CI 0.80–0.92)和良好神经功能预后率(aOR 0.84;95% CI 0.76–0.92)相关。 讨论部分指出,总体BCPR率稳定但早期启动下降,可能与 bystander 对感染的恐惧和不确定感导致的犹豫、居家限制使家庭内目击增加、家人目击者更依赖调度员指示后才开始按压等因素有关;疫情期间单纯胸外按压占比升高与含人工呼吸CPR减少也符合感染相关行为改变。SAA与非SAA的差异仅为亚组探索结果,且SAA属于政策代理指标而非疾病负担的直接测量,结论属于提出假设。研究建议将“目击至BCPR启动时间”纳入未来Utstein报告与登记基准,作为补充性质量指标。局限性包括目击与启动时间依赖旁观者回忆、目击时间仅为心脏骤停发生时间的替代、缺少调度员指令具体时机与CPR质量信息、可能存在未测量混杂,以及结果向其他国家推广受限。 研究结论翻译为:尽管疫情期间总体BCPR率未发生变化,时间-事件分析发现早期BCPR启动出现轻微下降。早期BCPR与更好的结局相关,但启动时机的差异并不能完全解释疫情期间较低的生存率。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! 从2000到2026,27载全因有您;您的每一分支持,都给予我们无穷的动力! records.content: Buchanan Secures Closure of COVID-19 Tuition Reimbursement Class Action for Wilkes University PHILADELPHIA (October 15, 2026) – Buchanan Ingersoll & Rooney’s Higher Education practice group secured the dismissal of a class action against client Wilkes University. The suit sought tuition and fee reimbursement on behalf of a proposed class of students. Rather than settle, as many peer institutions have in similar cases, Wilkes worked with George Morrison, shareholder and Higher Education practice group co-leader, and Krista Rose, associate in the firm’s Litigation section, to pursue an aggressive strategy that challenged the viability of the plaintiff’s claims at every stage. Colleges and universities across the country have paid millions of dollars to settle class actions brought by students seeking tuition and fee refunds after the shift to remote instruction during the COVID-19 pandemic. Filed against hundreds of institutions, these cases alleged that students were owed refunds because they did not receive the on-campus experience they paid for. The resulting wave of litigation has placed a heavy financial burden on higher education, with many institutions choosing to settle rather than face the cost and uncertainty of protracted litigation. Buchanan took a different approach, and it worked. In response to the vigorous defense mounted on behalf of Wilkes, the plaintiff abandoned the class claims entirely. The matter is now closed, and Wilkes avoided the millions of dollars in exposure that institutions of comparable size have paid to resolve similar cases. “This outcome shows the value of a determined, strategic defense in higher education litigation,” said Morrison. “The settlement trend in COVID-19 tuition cases has led plaintiffs to expect institutions to capitulate. The result in Como v. Wilkes University demonstrates that aggressive advocacy can produce a far better outcome for institutions willing to stand firm.” Buchanan’s Higher Education practice group counsels colleges and universities on the full range of legal challenges they face today, including class action defense, regulatory compliance, Title IX matters, faculty and staff employment disputes, student affairs litigation, and governance issues. The team understands the operational and reputational pressures unique to higher education and brings both strategic vision and hands-on litigation experience to every engagement. Our attorneys have successfully defended institutions of all sizes against high-exposure claims, and the group is committed to helping clients protect their missions and financial well-being

“畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 背景:A族链球菌(group A Streptococcus,GAS)感染的时序变化在全球范围内已有报道,但来自台湾的长期数据仍然有限。本研究评估了GAS感染的时间模式、年龄特异性疾病特征、抗菌药物敏感性以及与侵袭性GAS感染相关的因素。 方法:研究人员开展了一项回顾性研究,纳入了2015年至2024年间台湾某三级转诊中心的GAS感染患者。描述了每月医院确诊病例数,并采用多变量逻辑回归分析(multivariable logistic regression)来识别与侵袭性疾病相关的因素。 结果:在454例患者中,33例(7.3%)为侵袭性感染。每月病例数在COVID-19疫情期间(2020–2022年)显著下降,2023年仍维持低位,2024年增加至45例,但仍低于疫情前年度水平。≥65岁的成人占33例侵袭性病例中的14例(42.4%)。年龄≥18岁(调整后优势比[aOR],11.6;95%置信区间[CI],4.4–30.9;p < 0.001)以及存在两个或以上基础疾病类别(aOR,29.7;95% CI,10.4–84.5;p < 0.001)与侵袭性疾病相关。所有分离株均对青霉素敏感。侵袭性分离株对克林霉素和红霉素的敏感性较高,但对四环素的敏感性低于非侵袭性分离株。 结论:医院确诊的GAS病例显示出显著的时序变化。较高年龄和更大的基础疾病负担与侵袭性感染相关。这些发现可能为临床风险评估和机构监测提供支持。 一、研究背景与目的 高智能的大小鼠模型定制服务&严格质控的大小鼠繁育,马上咨询,为你的实验加速领 取 A族链球菌(group A Streptococcus,GAS)即化脓性链球菌(Streptococcus pyogenes),是全球范围内重要的人类病原体,每年估计导致约50万例死亡。其临床疾病谱广泛,既包括咽炎、脓疱疮、猩红热和蜂窝织炎等非侵袭性感染,也包括链球菌中毒性休克综合征(streptococcal toxic shock syndrome,STSS)、坏死性筋膜炎和脓毒症菌血症等侵袭性GAS疾病(invasive GAS disease,iGAS)。在COVID-19疫情期间,非药物干预措施与GAS感染的显著下降相关,多国报告了历史低位的发病率;而在防疫措施放松后,多地区GAS感染迅速反弹并超过疫情前水平,并伴随季节性变化和临床严重程度的增加。然而,台湾地区疫情后GAS感染的流行病学变化尚不明确。此前一项研究显示,2000年至2019年间台湾GAS感染中猩红热占比从54.8%显著升至77.9%,大环内酯类耐药率亦显著上升。鉴于台湾地区疫情后GAS流行病学数据的缺乏,研究人员在台湾大学医学院附设医院(National Taiwan University Hospital)这一北部三级转诊中心开展了2015年至2024年的回顾性研究,旨在评估GAS感染的时间与季节性模式、年龄特异性疾病分布及侵袭性感染的相关因素,为风险分层和疫情后监测策略提供依据。 二、主要技术方法 本研究为单中心回顾性研究,纳入2015年1月至2024年12月期间在该院确诊的化脓性链球菌感染患者,临床资料来源于电子病历系统。细菌鉴定采用基质辅助激光解吸电离飞行时间质谱(MALDI-TOF MS),抗菌药物敏感性检测采用VITEK系统并按临床和实验室标准协会(CLSI)标准判读,红霉素耐药而克林霉素敏感的菌株通过D-zone试验评估诱导型克林霉素耐药。感染按部位和严重程度分为上呼吸道感染、耳鼻窦感染、皮肤软组织感染和侵袭性感染四类。统计分析采用描述性统计、卡方检验或Fisher精确检验、Mann–Whitney U检验,并以多变量逻辑回归分析识别侵袭性疾病的独立相关因素。 三、研究结果 1. GAS感染的时间趋势与月度分布 研究期间共识别454例GAS感染病例。2015–2019年间月度病例数波动,年度总数分别为112、74、55、77和58例,无一致的季节性高峰月份。在预设的COVID-19期间(2020年1月1日至2022年12月31日),2020年3月后月度病例数急剧下降,2020年25例中17例(68.0%)发生在1–3月,2021–2022年仅识别5例。2023年仅3例,均出现在1月或2月。2024年病例数回升至45例,但仍低于疫情前各年度水平,且全年均有分布,年末增加并于12月达到9例的峰值。年-月热图显示各年月度分布存在显著的年际异质性。 2. 临床特征与年龄特异性疾病谱 总体队列中位年龄为6岁(IQR 5–9.25),侵袭性疾病患者年龄显著更大(中位56岁 vs. 6岁,p < 0.001)。≥65岁患者占侵袭性病例的42.4%,而仅占非侵袭性病例的1.0%;大多数非侵袭性感染发生于5–17岁儿童(70.8%)。上呼吸道感染在年轻年龄组中占主导,尤其在5–17岁儿童中占80.7%;侵袭性疾病在18–64岁成人中占21.7%,在≥65岁患者中高达77.8%。耳鼻窦感染几乎仅见于儿科患者。各年龄组疾病谱分布差异显著(p < 0.001)。 3. 侵袭性疾病的相关因素 多变量逻辑回归分析显示,年龄≥18岁(aOR,11.6;95% CI,4.4–30.9;p < 0.001)和存在两个及以上基础疾病类别(aOR,29.7;95% CI,10.4–84.5;p < 0.001)是侵袭性疾病的独立相关因素。侵袭性病例中63.6%存在两个及以上基础疾病类别,而非侵袭性病例中该比例仅为2.6%。 4. 抗菌药物敏感性 所有分离株均对青霉素敏感。侵袭性分离株对克林霉素和红霉素的敏感性显著高于非侵袭性分离株(72.7% vs. 51.1%,p = 0.02;69.7% vs. 51.1%,p = 0.04),而对四环素的敏感性较低(27.3% vs. 51.8%,p = 0.01)。左氧氟沙星敏感性两组间无显著差异。 四、讨论与结论 研究人员观察到GAS病例在COVID-19期间显著下降、2024年部分回升但未达疫情前水平,且未呈现一致的冬季高峰模式,这与部分国际研究中2022–23年短暂激增后回归基线的趋势不同。可能的机制包括“免疫债”假说、医疗资源利用和检测实践变化以及呼吸道病毒共同流行等,但均需进一步研究验证。年龄和基础疾病负担是侵袭性感染的重要风险因素,与既往文献一致。侵袭性与非侵袭性分离株间抗菌药物敏感性的差异可能涉及特定克隆的扩张,如携带erm(B)和tet(M)的emm12-ST36,但本研究未进行分子分型,相关解释仍属推测。研究存在回顾性设计、单中心、侵袭性病例数较少、依赖ICD编码识别基础疾病及缺乏分子分型等局限性。总体而言,医院确诊GAS病例在COVID-19期间下降并于2024年回升,侵袭性感染与较高年龄及两个以上基础疾病类别相关,这些发现可为临床风险评估和机构监测提供支持。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪!
